name: U.S. Copyright Office: Artificial Intelligence Study policy page
title: U.S. Copyright Office: Artificial Intelligence Study policy page
answer: This is the U.S. Copyright Office landing page for its artificial intelligence study, which collects information and policy views on copyright and AI. Its most useful content is a dated record of the study's published parts: Part 1 on digital replicas, published 31 July 2024, Part 2 on the copyrightability of generative AI outputs, published 29 January 2025, and a pre-publication Part 3 released 9 May 2025, with a final version promised later and no substantive changes expected.

sections.body: It is a policy page published by the U.S. Copyright Office, a government body, describing its artificial intelligence study. The page sets out the purpose of the study and lists the parts of the resulting Report published so far, with dates. It is a short signpost page rather than the study itself, and it does not reproduce the analysis contained in the Report parts. The page was harvested on 26 September 2026, and the most recent item it mentions is the pre-publication version of Part 3 released on 9 May 2025.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The U.S. Copyright Office states that it is conducting a study of the copyright issues raised by artificial intelligence. The study collects information and policy views relevant to copyright law and policy. The Office says it will use that material to analyse the current state of the law, identify unresolved issues, and evaluate potential areas for congressional action. The page then lists what the study has published so far. Part 1 of the Report, published on 31 July 2024, addresses digital replicas. Part 2, published on 29 January 2025, addresses the copyrightability of outputs created using generative AI. On 9 May 2025 the Office released a pre-publication version of Part 3, which it describes as a response to congressional inquiries and expressions of interest from stakeholders. The Office states that a final version of Part 3 will be published in the future, and that no substantive changes to the analysis or conclusions are expected. The page gives no further detail on what Part 3 contains, and no date for the final version.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source gives three dates and three subject areas. Part 1 of the Report was published on 31 July 2024 and addresses digital replicas. Part 2 was published on 29 January 2025 and addresses the copyrightability of outputs created using generative AI. A pre-publication version of Part 3 was released on 9 May 2025 in response to congressional inquiries and stakeholder interest. The Office also states that the final Part 3 will not differ substantively in analysis or conclusions from the pre-publication version.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in media publishing would use this page to track the stage the Copyright Office has reached, and to find the parts of the Report that deal with digital replicas and with the copyrightability of generative AI outputs. Those two topics bear directly on how AI-assisted media is registered and protected in the United States. The page is useful as a dated index and as confirmation that the Office frames its work around unresolved issues and possible congressional action, but it is not itself a statement of the Office's legal positions.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Media

sections.body: This is a landing page with little substance. It summarises the study's purpose and lists publication dates, but it does not reproduce any of the Report's analysis, definitions or conclusions. It does not itself address training on copyrighted material, which the industry page citing it mentions, and it gives no date for the final Part 3. It offers no compliance guidance and no view on how the law applies to particular uses. It is a government page rather than commercial material, and it is partial in the sense that the study is still in progress.
